title: Remaining work & limitations (for the next session(s))
limit: Ordered by value. Each item is self-contained enough to start immediately.

items.title: Daily automated collection (needs a networked runner)
items.detail: scripts/collect-kalshi.mjs is written and unit-scaffolded, but this session's sandbox had no general internet, so it could not be exercised live. Run it in CI (workflow committed: .github/workflows/daily-collection.yml, disabled until the collector is proven) to accumulate: full open-market universe (paginated GET /markets), order books, candlestick histories for every new market, and the historical tier as markets settle. Every artifact must carry capturedFrom+capturedAt or the lint fails.
items.why: Forward collection is the user's explicit requirement ('internally model/forecast via historical data collection + backtesting + forward collection') and the 2026 live-cycle evidence base grows daily.

items.title: 2024 per-state Senate race markets (series tickers not yet identified)
items.detail: This session verified the PRES, CONTROLH and CONTROLS series (2024 settled + 2026/2028 live). The per-state 2024 Senate tickers (e.g. a 2024 Arizona market) were not found by guessing; the API has no public search endpoint. Next step: enumerate GET /historical/markets by event-ticker pattern or mine kalshi.com slugs for 2024 Senate pages, capture candlesticks, and extend the multi-market backtest from 3 to ~40 markets. This is the single biggest backtest-power upgrade.
items.why: A 3-market backtest can detect gross miscalibration but not state-level structure (incumbency, partisans, toss-up buckets).

items.title: 2026 forward-collection loop with a live calibration tracker
items.detail: Once R1 runs daily: (a) store the implied probability of every open 2026 market each day; (b) as markets settle (first: LA mayor Nov 3, 2026), compute Brier/log-loss per market and per calibration bucket; (c) publish the running record on this site. This directly tests the exchange's '70% means 70%' claim on forward data and the contest's theses on 2026 markets.
items.why: Turns the project from a 2024 retrospective into a live, scored forecasting operation — the user's 'track expected vs actual results' requirement.

items.title: Poll layer beyond 538: add VoteHub/RCP daily averages and the Quinnipiac 2026 series
items.detail: The poll backtest currently uses only the archived 538 national averages (ends 2024-09-12). Adding RCP's daily averages (archived per election) and the 2026 Quinnipiac/other releases (verified in data/polls/verified-polls.json) would give a continuous 2026 poll-vs-market spread to test poll-anchor style strategies on live markets.
items.why: The 2024 result (polls -4.3pp miss, market closer) is a single-cycle observation; a 2026 replication would make it a finding.

items.title: Cross-market consistency checks as a standing monitor
items.detail: Codify: (a) D+R book complementarity per event (flags like #7), (b) monotone outcome sets (flag #8), (c) Kalshi-vs-Polymarket divergence alerts (>5pp on the same event), (d) web-% vs API-book divergence (flag #2). Output to data/discrepancy-watch.json each collect run.
items.why: Cheap to compute, and each catch is a published data-quality result — the 'flag discrepancies' requirement operationalized.

items.title: 2020 cycle extension (markets did not exist; poll archive does)
items.detail: Add a 2020 poll-only backtest row (538 2020 averages in the same archive) with the verified official outcome (Biden 306 EV; 81,283,501 votes) to test poll calibration across a wave year vs 2024. No Kalshi markets existed then (exchange launched 2021) — state that explicitly.
items.why: Multi-cycle poll error distribution is what the user asked for ('backtest polls and predictions against actual verified outcomes').

items.title: Strategy population growth + tournament structure
items.detail: Add entrants with distinct theories (e.g., incumbent-defender on Senate series, seat-count-basis-arb, volatility-scaling) and a 2-cycle cumulative PnL ranking once 2026 settles. Keep The Leap conventions ($100k, realized PnL ranking, min-trading-days rule: require >=3 trading days to be ranked).
items.why: The 'competition' is the user's explicit framing; a single 2024 cycle is a pilot, not a tournament.

items.title: Documentation hardening
items.detail: VERIFICATION.md currently covers the 2026-09-18 session; each session should append its own dated section (what was fetched, line-by-line notes, hashes of copied files). Add SHA-256 hashes of the CSV copies in data/polls/PROVENANCE.md to make byte-level integrity checkable.
items.why: No-hallucination standard: provenance must be auditable by a third party without network access.

limitations: Sandbox of the 2026-09-18 session had no general internet: live capture was done via a proxy fetch tool, so only the manually enumerated endpoints (documented per file) were captured; the full open-market universe awaits R1.
2024 backtest universe = 3 markets (presidency + both chamber controls). Directionally strong (all settled YES on the R side, matching official outcomes), statistically thin.
NO-side prices in captured candles are derived reciprocals (1 - yesClose); the raw API only publishes the YES-side candle history for these series.
Poll data for 2024 ends 2024-09-12 (538 archive cutoff); the poll-vs-market comparison after that date reuses the anchor with its age disclosed.
Web-rendered percentages (kalshi.com hub) are a display convenience; where the API book was captured, that is the authoritative figure and divergences are flagged (IRREGULARITIES #2, #7).
GitHub Pages serves the committed src/data/site-data.js; the site is a snapshot of 2026-09-18 until the next build commit.
